title: "What is the point of lifting natty past 30 if test levels crash?"
summary: Answering a viewer who asks why stay natural past 30 if testosterone declines, he argues that stopping training loses muscle faster, that planning only to maintain becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy, and that muscle is your lifeline for mobility in old age. He doubts testosterone-decline studies apply to healthy athletes, says strength athletes peak at 35-40 and testosterone declines slowly, and adds that even if gains vanished at 30 you should still be your best now. Natural is the only reliable long-term path.

claims.claim: Even if gains slowly decline after 30, stopping training loses them much faster (within about 2 years or less), so continuing is clearly better.
Deciding you can only maintain after 30 makes you cut volume or intensity until stagnation is all that happens: a self-fulfilling prophecy.
Muscle is your lifeline: people lose the ability to walk when they lack musculature in the glutes, hamstrings and quads; more muscle as you age keeps you mobile and active in a virtuous circle.
The age at which people say their bodies stop working keeps dropping (50s, then 40s, 30s, now 20s); peers his age have bad backs because they lack an active mentality and expect decline.
He is skeptical of testosterone-decline studies because the subjects may have poor lifestyles; he'd want a study following athletic, whole-food-eating, sober men sleeping 8 hours from 20 to 35+.
His 91-year-old grandfather still works in the fields for hours daily, and men in his mountain village stay physically active into their 60s and 70s thanks to lifelong physical work.
Continuing to accumulate volume and tonnage year after year not only maintains muscle but can keep it growing.
He rejects the idea that strength and tonnage can rise while muscles shrink; neural adaptation only goes so far, after which strength depends on muscle size (depending on leverages).
Most past Olympic weightlifters and powerlifters peaked at 35-40, which he says is when male maximal strength occurs.
He claims total testosterone (excluding the puberty spike) peaks around 35-40 for most men and then declines slowly rather than crashing, with major drops only in the 60s-70s for some men.
Training through your 20s, or from your teens, builds an environment for growth so you can be at your best in your prime and stay near the top.
Even if all your muscle vanished at 30, you should still live fully and make the best gains you can before that.
Natural bodybuilding is the only reliable long-term approach; with PEDs you never know what can happen, and life already has enough obstacles.
At 25 he feels he is just getting started on a long road.

viewer_questions: What is the point of staying natural after 30 if testosterone declines every year?
